 U.S. news Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders take legal action against My Chemical Romance over onstage costumes
 Dancers at the band’s Hollywood Bowl concert this week wore outfits that appeared nearly identical to the cheerleaders’ iconic white and blue uniforms, a court filing said. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders in Arlington, Texas. Sam Hodde / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 24, 2026, 11:43 AM EDT By Matt Lavietes The parent company of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders is taking legal action against My Chemical Romance after the band performed alongside dancers in costumes resembling the iconic cheerleading team’s uniforms this week.
 Pro Silver Star, which owns the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders brand, filed a motion for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction Friday in district court in Dallas County, Texas, seeking to bar the alternative rock band from using the costumes onstage.
 My Chemical Romance, best known for its 2000s hits “Teenagers” and “Welcome to the Black Parade,” performed Wednesday at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles with dancers wearing outfits that appeared nearly identical to the squad’s iconic white and blue uniforms, according to the court filing.
 The dancers carried what appeared to be rifles and engaged in a staged firefight, “only to be depicted being shot,” the filing states.
 “Audience members and online commentators understandably believed that the performers were the real Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and said so in social media posts that continue to circulate,” Pro Silver Star wrote.
 The company said it was “not litigious” and “takes no issue with MCR’s music, its artistic ambitions, or any message Defendants seek to convey.”
